title: Approximate Caching for Efficiently Serving Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
abstract: Text-to-image generation using diffusion models has seen explosive popularity owing to their ability in producing high quality images adhering to text prompts. However, diffusionmodels go through a large number of iterative denoising steps, and are resource-intensive, requiring expensive GPUs and incurring considerable latency. In this paper, we introduce a novel approximate-caching technique that can reduce such iterative denoising steps by reusing intermediate noise states created during a prior image generation. Based on this idea, we present an end-to-end text-to-image generation system, N IRVANA , that uses approximate-caching with a novel cache management policy to provide 21% GPU compute savings, 19.8% end-to-end latency reduction, and 19% dollar savings on two real production workloads. We further present an extensive characterization of real production text-to-image prompts from the perspective of caching, popularity and reuse of intermediate states in a large production environment.
